Class Turtle

java.lang.Object
Turtle
All Implemented Interfaces:
ActionListener, ComponentListener, KeyListener, MouseListener, MouseMotionListener, MouseWheelListener, Runnable, EventListener
public final class Turtle extends Object implements Runnable, ActionListener, MouseListener, MouseMotionListener, KeyListener, ComponentListener, MouseWheelListener
Allows students to make beautiful turtle graphics with ease.

    • run

      public void run()
      Renders the turtles and listens for key presses. This method is run in two separate threads, one for rendering and one for listening. You should not call this method directly.

    • refreshMode

      public static void refreshMode(int mode)
      This specifies when the screen gets refreshed. 0(default)=Animated (The turtle will slide from one state to another without being jerky.) 1=State Change (The turtle will refresh immediately to the last state. Jerky motion.) 2=On Demand (The turtle will refresh only when you call update())
      Parameters:
      mode - refresh mode

    • backgroundMode

      public static void backgroundMode(int mode)
      This specifies how the background is drawn. 0=The image if present is stretched to fill the screen. 1=The image is centered on the middle of the screen and will not scale/pan 2=The image is tiled and will not scale/pan 3=The image is centered on (0,0) and will scale/pan 4(default)=The image is tiled and will scale/pan
      Parameters:
      mode - background mode

    • onKey

      public boolean onKey(String methodName, String keyText)

      Links a method to a key. Simply pass in the name of a method inside of the class that's calling this method. The method must either take in a Turtle object or a String as a parameter and should return void

      Parameters:
      methodName - method to be executed when the key is pressed
      keyText - key that triggers the method
      Returns:
      true if the method was successfully linked to the key, false if the method doesn't exist or has the wrong signature.

    • onKey

      public boolean onKey(String methodName, String keyText, boolean append)

      Links a method to a key. Simply pass in the name of a method inside of the class that's calling this method. The method must either take in a Turtle object or a String as a parameter and should return void

      Parameters:
      methodName - method to be executed when the key is pressed
      keyText - key that triggers the method
      append - true if you want to have multiple methods per key
      Returns:
      true if the method was successfully linked to the key, false if the method doesn't exist or has the wrong signature.

    • onKey

      public boolean onKey(String methodName, String keyText, boolean append, boolean repeat)

      Links a method to a key. Simply pass in the name of a method inside of the class that's calling this method. The method must either take in a Turtle object or a String as a parameter and should return void

      Parameters:
      methodName - method to be executed when the key is pressed
      keyText - key that triggers the method
      append - true if you want to have multiple methods per key
      repeat - true if you want call the method every screen refresh
      Returns:
      true if the method was successfully linked to the key, false if the method doesn't exist or has the wrong signature.

    • approxCollidesWith

      public boolean approxCollidesWith(Turtle other, boolean circular)

      Determines if this turtle approximately collides with another turtle using approximate hitboxes. - If circular is true, uses two circles to determine collision. - Else, uses two rectangles to determine collision. Both collision detection methods center the shape at the turtle's location and uses the turtle's shape width and height multiplied by the scale factor to determine the size of the shape.

      Parameters:
      other - the turtle to check collision with
      circular - if true, uses circular collision detection. If false, uses rectangular collision detection.
      Returns:
      true if the turtles collide, false otherwise
